Valve's well-made Steam Deck teardown showing openness about internals

comments.author: bspammer
comments.story: Valve opens up a Steam Deck to explain why it thinks you shouldn’t
comments.why: Pro-consumer teardown that treats viewers like adults
comments.text: You need to watch the video: [VIDEO] I haven't seen anything so pro-consumer from a major electronics manufacturer in years. It's so refreshing being talked to like an adult with agency.

comments.author: druidsbane
comments.story: Take a look inside Steam Deck!
comments.why: Valve's well-made Steam Deck teardown showing openness about internals
comments.text: The "teardown" video was quite well done: [VIDEO] . Their openness is an interesting contrast with other manufacturers.

comments.author: dorveille
comments.why: Shows SSD replacement and why storage capacity is heat-limited
comments.text: This right here is the core of the matter. When a Valve provides a detailed guide to replacing the SSD if you really want to, I trust the devs when they say we wanted to have higher storage capacities but heat dissipation was the constraining factor. [VIDEO] You want a Samsung PM991a, a Sabrent Rocket SB-2130-1TB, or a Kioxia BG4, to keep the draw as close to 1 amp as possible. Or slay your battery and bake your internals. It's your hardware, do what you want.

comments.author: chaorace
comments.story: Microsoft posts its own teardown and repair video for the Surface Laptop SE
comments.why: Valve's Deck teardown as precedent for manufacturers showing internals
comments.text: I wonder if this was influenced by Valve's recent "Deck" teardown video?[1] I'd love to see this become a trend in the "boutique" hardware space -- it's a lot harder to cut corners on the internals when you're shining a spotlight on them! [1]: [VIDEO]
